Sophie's Curse, um jogo de terror feito pelo (ou pelos) mesmo cara (caras), que fizeram aquele jogo do vizinho maluco das ideias, mas este jogo da Sophie veio primeiro que aquele do vizinho.

Não há muito o que falar sobre esse jogo, a história para eu ter pego esse jogo é o mesmo da do jogo do vizinho, eu vi muitas vezes o Alan (Alanzoka) jogando esses jogos, e eu adorava assistir, e tive muita vontade de jogar quando eu via. Mas agora que eu tenho a possibilidade de jogar (e joguei, só não cheguei a terminar), eu jogo e simplesmente não tenho vontade de continuar... 

No entanto, vamos falar um pouquinho sobre esse jogo. Sophie's Curse é um jogo de terror de point clicker, que você tem que sobreviver desde um tal horário até outro horário (esqueci de quanto em quanto tempo que é o jogo). Você terá de sobreviver e "cuidar" de um senhor de idade enquanto a Sophie irá tentar te matar. A história do jogo é bem bolada e bem contada na verdade, e possui uma mecânica de gameplay cativante e interessante, os sustos desse jogo são sensacional, e imprevisíveis até você aprender e entender o porque de estar morrendo e tomando esses sustos. Porém, o jogo é bem simples, pode de início dar a impressão de ser um jogo complicado e difícil, mas quando você aprende sobre o que você deve fazer e tals, perde o medo e um pouco da graça.

Nota final: 6/10

Sophie’s Curse is from an era of small indie horror games that came and never really left. A short point-and-click horror experience focused around one or two game mechanics and a big spooky monster. It is nothing to shy from when you are looking to make a game, and quite a few of them out there manage to create memorable experiences. Although Sophie’s Curse is not really what you could call a “bad” game, it is hardly worth a recommendation. It must have been a nice experience for the developer and the people that found its proposal worth their time, and I wish all of them more of those. But taking into account all the good games there are out there, especially this cheap, I cannot really encourage you to play it.

Aesthetically speaking, there is nothing that really stands out about Sophie’s Curse. It is not a very pretty game and does not strike me as very unique. For starters, it is hard to understand what the black borders all around the screen, or the choppy frame rate of the transitions between each location are meant to accomplish. It could be that the goal was to create an aesthetic of its own, but it feels more jarring than anything and makes the game look dated even for its time. Aside from that, there is nothing very interesting about the environment itself, you are in a regular house after all, one that is supposed to be lived in. I would say that the lighting can create interesting moments were it not for the soundscape that spoils each apparition of the monster. Speaking of which, Sophie is nothing really special either. She’s a ghost of some sort who looks like a corpse. There is nothing particularly striking about her either. You’ve seen this monster a hundred times now on the internet.

So, Sophie’s Curse is a point-and-click; what else? Well, you are in a spooky house to look after an elderly man who’s already asleep. But really, what motivates you to be here is that you are looking for ghosts with your pal Henry, who will be messaging you from time to time on the computer in the kitchen. It’s not clear what the two of you want to accomplish, especially since Henry tells you about Sophie like you have never heard about her before coming here. Anyhow, there is some lighting equipment lying around the house that needs recharging. If one light goes out of battery, the whole system goes into shutdown and needs to reboot, leaving you vulnerable. So, you have to keep the lights on, but not too much. Sophie’s going to get angry if you do it in her face, which you’ll hear from time to time. This forces you to listen carefully and avoid doing anything for a few seconds. Lights can glitch, forcing you to solve a mini game on the computer to reset them before a timer goes off. Finally, Sophie can get curious enough to get a good look at you, at which point you’ll have to run in the opposite direction. You have to survive these hazards from 7PM to 7AM. The gameplay would be fine were it not for the fact most of these mechanics seem to overlap in contradicting ways. Sophie can appear just as the timer was going off or a light was about to run out of juice, resetting the whole thing. It makes the game very easy and bombards you with useless information more than it overwhelms you with stressful tasks. It is also quite buggy sometimes. Sophie can still get you even if you run the opposite way because you might have triggered the jump scare at the same time you begining to run away.

Sound-wise, I do not have nice things to say about the game. It being a jump scare-fest is already an uphill battle with most people’s enjoyment of a horror game, but this one really goes below the belt. Your cue that Sophie is around is usually a very faint sound of her breathing, forcing you to keep listening closely. Of course, that’s just so the game can startle you easier when she does show up in front of you, or kills you, with a big screamer. It’s not scary, it’s not original, and you’ll get more annoyed each time it happens. Other than that, the lack of music and the abundance of sounds that seem to be stock effects doesn’t help to create something memorable.

That’s what there is to say about Sophie’s Curse overall. It’s not a bad experience because it’s an awful game per say. But it misses the mark because it doesn’t really want to be anything more than a spooky horror game that uses the most conventional and cliché techniques the genre was full of at the time it came out. It’s only a small game that probably got the developer some attention, and that’s what matters in the end. Hopefully they made some better, more heartfelt games later on!

I was hoping I'd like this game, but it just doesn't seem to play by its own rules. Basically, this game plays similar to FNAF, but instead of you mostly being in one spot, you're running around a house keeping lights on (if you've played FNAF2, it's like if the music box was the only part of the game, and there's four of them). The game states that while you're recharging a light and you hear Sophie make a sound, you need to stop charging it immediately. Well, even if you do, it seems completely random on whether she decides to kill you or not. She kills if you stop charging quickly, if you don't move, and even if you DO move. I swear it's complete RNG whether or not she kills you when you hear her while you charge a light. It almost feels like every checkpoint of the game has a 'death quota' or something. So the game went from entertaining to VERY annoying quickly. I also think it's kind of funny that the game wants you to simultaneously move quickly, but don't move too quickly, because Sophie might be where you're going and if you click on her you'll die.

As for the good points of the game, I think the game looks good, and the animations for Sophie's actions are good. I do wish the room transition animations were a little quicker, though, especially for when the lights start to flicker and you have to find your safe spot (which I THINK only changes after every time the power goes out, the game isn't very clear on when it moves). I also kind of appreciate that after the lights flicker they're all practically recharged, so there's less stress for a second.

If you're thinking of getting this, I can really only recommend getting it on a sale. And best of luck on the Curse of Sophie's RNG.

Das ist der selbe Blödsinn wie FNAF nur etwas besser. 
Aber auch hier hat man es wieder mit sehr monotonen Gameplay zu tun. Man hat eine Aufgabe, drehe die Kurbeln. Mit so was holt man mich einfach nicht ab. Die Schreckmomente werden hier durch die billigst möglichen In-Your-Face-Jumpscares erzeugt, die seit über 10 Jahren langweilig und abgenutzt sind.
Die Bewegungsmechanik ist ebenso altbacken wie die Scares. Man kann sich nicht normal mit wasd bewegen, nein, man spielt das Game nur mit der Maus. Man klickt auf den Bildschirm um sich zu bewegen. Diese Mechanik haben Spiele wie "11th Hours" und "7th Guest" in den frühen 90'ern mal eingeführt und die sind schnell veraltet. War halt  in der Anfangszeit der 3D Spiele und da haben die Leute mal rum probiert. In modernen Spielen hat das nichts mehr zu suchen. 
Für Fans von FNAF oder Retro-Games kann das hier vielleicht noch was sein. Aber es ist halt abgenutzter und 20 mal recycelter Kram, der keinen Horror Fan mehr abholen sollte. 
Ich finde auch, die Spielfigur atmet viel zu laut. Hat der eine Lungenkranheit oder so? Kann auch sein, dass er eine Gasmaske trägt. Auf jeden Fall hört man dadurch Sophie echt sehr schlecht. Das Getöse von dem Gewitter macht es natürlich nicht besser^^. Aber das geht für die Atmosphäre schon noch gut klar. Weniger klar gehen die ganzen anderen Sachen, wie Gerumpel, Klirren und sonstiges. Es ist immer irgendwas und ich wusste nie, wann ich nun wirklich vorsichtig sein muss.  Das war einfach genau so eine Reizüberfutung wie bei Project Nightmares: Case 36 Henrietta Kedward. Das bewirkt bei mir genau das Gegenteil von dem was es eigentlich soll. Es zerstört die Atmosphäre und nach 5 Minuten ist kein Horror mehr möglich. Weniger ist halt oft doch mehr. vor allem sagt einem das Spiel ja: Achte auf auffällige Geräusche um nicht zu sterben. Aber wenn jede Sekunde ein anderes auffälliges Geräusch kommt? Für mich wurde das so eher zu einem Glücksspiel und ich bin 3 Mal kurz vor 120 gestorben, wo man dann den zweiten Checkpoint bekommt. Habe echt kein Bock Sachen immer und immer wieder zu machen. beim letzten Tod war ich direkt nach dem Lichtevent am Laptop um zu schauen, wo die nächste Savezone ist. Als ich den geschlossen habe, stand Sophie direkt vor mir und ist mir ins Gesicht gesprungen. Und wieder alles von vorne.  Es gab keine Anzeichen, dass sie da steht, kein Geräusch nichts.  Man braucht eine unglaublich hohe Frustschwelle für so ein Spiel und die ist bei mir eher sehr niedrig ;).

Thank you for a small bit of my Childhood!

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

"Sophie's Curse" ist ein First-Person-Horror-Spiel.

Am ehesten läßt sich das Spiel mit "Five Nights at Freddy´s" oder "Boogy Man" vergleichen. Wir sind in einem Haus und haben einen Laptop, der uns vier Orte zeigt, die jeweils eine Glühbirne haben, deren Generator mit einer Handkurbel wieder aufgeladen werden kann. Zwischen den einzelnen Orten können wir uns nicht etwa frei bewegen, sondern wechseln praktisch immer zwischen einzelnen Screens, indem wir an den Rand des vorherigen Screens scrollen oder auf den Bildschirm klicken. Das Bewegungsmodell ist ungewöhnlich und es braucht etwas sich daran zu gewöhnen. 

Die Glühbirnen verbrauchen immer wieder unterschiedlich viel Energie, so daß wir zwischen den Orten wechseln müssen, um die einzelnen Generatoren am Laufen zu halten. Währenddessen ist auch Sophie unterwegs, die uns nicht erwischen darf, sonst wird der Run mit einem Jumpscare beendet. Sie meldet sich durch bestimmte Vorzeichen wie Geräusche an, so daß wir theoretisch vor ihr fliehen können. 

Es gilt, mehrere Zeitabschnitte zu überstehen, in denen die Glühbirnen-Generatoren immer mehr Ausfälle haben und in denen Sophie immer aggressiver wird.

Bei ainem Ausfall eines Generators müssen wir zurück zum Laptop um den Generator über kleine Mini-Spiele wieder zu reparieren. Vor allem in späteren Leveln ist das Aufrechterhalten der Beleuchtung purer Streß. 

Die Grafik ist für einen Indie-Titel des Genres durchaus gelungen und auch die Sounds passen zum Genre.

Im Endeffekt ist das Spiel mechanisch sehr übersichtlich aufgebaut. Sehr wenige Orte und auch recht wenige Aktionsmöglichkeiten. Und trotzdem ist die Atmosphäre gut und die potentielle Angst vorhanden.

[u][b]ソフィー(幽霊)との命がけの一夜[/b][/u]

クリック操作のみで遊べる疑似3Dホラーゲーム。びっくりする描写多め。
日本語非対応なので、ルール等は翻訳されたものを探して読んだ方がよいかも。

主人公は、ソフィーという名前の幽霊が憑りついた屋敷で一晩を過ごすことになる。
屋敷には計4つのライトが設置されており、消えないように手回しで充電して朝を待つ。

ソフィーは様々な方法でこちらを妨害してくるが対処法はゲーム中で詳しく説明されない。
そのため、何度も死にながら法則性を探す必要がある。
これは人によっては理不尽に感じるかと思うが、個人的にはなかなか楽しい過程だと感じた。
ただし、後半に近づくにつれて電池の減り方、妨害の発生頻度が増え、
同じことの繰り返し・運ゲー感が増えてしまうのはいまいちな点か。

値段に比して楽しめるゲームで、やりごたえはかなりあると感じた。
一方で、ホラー要素を期待して買うと驚かせ方にパターンがないのでがっかりするかも。
